title: Redwood POC scoping with Parkway Medical - security pilot
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on security and compliance requirements for a 3-month pilot: SOC 2 / ISO paperwork, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logs, KMS key ownership, and performance benchmarks. Agreed to run a 3-day benchmark on dedicated capacity and share security pack and SSO docs. Timeline target: benchmark start 2027-12-20, pricing and pilot contract by 2027-12-17.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna run through the POC scope for the security pilot with Parkway. quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Sara Patel: Hi, Sara here, head of data at Parkway.
[00:15] Marcus Lee: Marcus, infra engineer, i'll be running the bench env.
[00:18] Elena Gomez: Elena, CISO, I'll be driving the security checklist.
[00:22] Alex Chen: Great. Priya from our side?
[00:24] Priya Raman: hey all, Priya SE on infra/perf. i'll own the benchmark runs and perf details.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Cool. high level why you're running the pilot? Sara?
[00:35] Dr. Sara Patel: we're looking at embedding an LLM inside our clinical triage workflow for internal summarizations and some coding. must be private, must meet compliance — SOC 2 or ISO, plus SSO for employees, strict RBAC, audit logs, and data retention controls.
[00:52] Alex Chen: totally. for the POC we're proposing a 3-month pilot but first we do a 3-day benchmark to verify perf and cost assumptions. Priya, correct me if i'm off.
[01:03] Priya Raman: yeah, plan is: run a 72-hour benchmark against a dev dataset that Marcus will provide (sanitized). profile: 1M tokens/day simulated peak pattern, 75 p95 latency target < 400ms for 256-token requests, and sustained throughput target ~20 req/s. those are initial numbers we talked about — can adjust.
[01:26] Marcus Lee: 1M tokens/day sounds fine as a pilot upper bound. question — dedicated infra or Redwood private? we need to decide because security requirements vary.
[01:35] Elena Gomez: our preference is private VPC if possible. we need to own keys (KMS/HSM) or at least a BYOK option, and we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence up front. also SAML SSO integration and RBAC so we can map AD groups.
[01:52] Alex Chen: Understood. Redwood offers multiple deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, and private VPC/on-prem. For security pilots we typically do Dedicated with VPC peering or Redwood Private depending on legal. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools but keys can be managed by Redwood; Private gives you customer-managed KMS. We'll put this clearly in the doc.
[02:12] Dr. Sara Patel: can you clarify the differences? are we losing anything performance-wise if we choose private?
[02:18] Priya Raman: performance is similar; private might have slightly higher network RTT depending on your peering. compute kernels are the same. main diff is control of keys, network egress policies, and audit access. we can run the 3-day benchmark on dedicated first, then move the same config to private if needed.
[02:34] Elena Gomez: we also need full audit logs with immutable retention for 1 year and the ability to export logs to our Splunk/SIEM. is that supported?
[02:45] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood provides audit logs, request/response metadata, and admin actions. exports to S3 or syslog are supported; we can also stream to Splunk. retention configurable — for the pilot we can set a 1-year retention, and we'll include a sample retention policy in the pack. note that response bodies are treated as data plane traffic and retention may have cost implications.
[03:05] Marcus Lee: about redaction — we need redaction pipelines for PHI. can Redwood do on-the-fly masking before storing logs?
[03:13] Priya Raman: we have options: prefix/KV caching and policy-based masking. for pilot we recommend instrumenting a pre-processing layer that strips PHI and uses tokenization to send minimal PII. we can show sample regex-based redaction.
[03:27] Dr. Sara Patel: success criteria from our side — accuracy threshold for summarization (ROUGE-like checks), latency p95 under 400ms for typical clinic prompts, and zero incidents of data exfil in pilot. Also SSO works end-to-end and RBAC maps to AD groups.
[03:45] Alex Chen: good — i'll capture those as success criteria: (1) functional quality — basic evals pass NPS/ROUGE thresholds, (2) perf — p95 < 400ms for 256-token context, throughput ~20 req/s sustained, (3) security — SOC2/ISO certs provided, SAML SSO integrated, RBAC enforced, audit logs exported, BYOK or equivalent KMS controls, (4) legal signoff within pilot window.
[04:10] Elena Gomez: on SSO: we use Okta. can you support SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning? we want group sync.
[04:20] Alex Chen: yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM supported. we'll share the SAML metadata and a SCIM user/group mapping doc. setup usually takes a day or two on your side.
[04:29] Marcus Lee: for the benchmark, what model variants will you run? quantized? full fp16?
[04:33] Priya Raman: we'll test both. start with an optimized open model variant in int8/q4 as a cost/perf baseline, then run a fp16 run for quality parity checks. kernels are tuned for continuous batching. we'll include tokenization script and latency harness.
[04:49] Dr. Sara Patel: any compliance paperwork we need before bench? pen test?
[04:53] Alex Chen: we can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs, plus our standard pen test summary. if you require a complete pen test or a third-party attestation specifically for this pilot, that's doable but will add time. for the pilot we typically share certs and the pen test executive summary.
[05:12] Elena Gomez: also need data residency notes — some patient data must stay in-region (US-East). can you guarantee region pinning?
[05:19] Priya Raman: yes, region pinning is supported for hosted/dedicated/private. we'll pin the pilot to US-East-1.
[05:24] Marcus Lee: about audit logs — do you capture request/response payloads or just metadata? we need payload-level logs in our SIEM but only after redaction rules.
[05:33] Alex Chen: both are possible. We can provide full request/response payload logs, but we'll capture them behind a retention & redaction policy. by default we ship metadata; payload capture is opt-in and we can stream to customer S3 with encryption.
[05:46] Dr. Sara Patel: timeline recap?
[05:48] Alex Chen: agreed proposed timeline: 12/16 — Redwood sends security pack (SOC2/ISO, pen test summary, SAML/SCIM docs, RBAC matrix). 12/17 — Redwood sends pilot commercial terms and pricing estimate. 12/20 — Start 3-day benchmark run (Priya to run with Marcus's dataset). 12/23 — Benchmark results & follow-up demo. 12/30 — decision point for 3-month pilot start. does that sound okay?
[06:12] Elena Gomez: that's fine but legal review may need until 12/22. we'll try to accelerate.
[06:17] Marcus Lee: i'll prepare a sanitized dataset and a throughput/failure scenario doc by 12/19.
[06:23] Priya Raman: perfect. i'll share the harness and scripts today.
[06:26] Alex Chen: any blockers?
[06:28] Dr. Sara Patel: just confirming BYOK — we need ability to rotate keys from our KMS.
[06:33] Alex Chen: yes, BYOK supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we offer a managed KMS with customer key import options. we'll detail the tradeoffs in the security pack.
[06:43] Elena Gomez: one more — RBAC: we want role separation between developers and clinical users; can you provide fine-grained roles?
[06:50] Priya Raman: we support admin, dev, analyst, and custom roles with attribute-based access controls. we'll include an example RBAC mapping for AD groups.
[06:58] Alex Chen: ok, let me recap next steps then.
[07:00] Alex Chen: ACTIONS: Alex to send SOC2/ISO and pen test summary by 12/16; Priya to share benchmark harness and run on 12/20; Marcus to supply sanitized dataset by 12/19; Elena to confirm legal timeline by 12/22. we'll schedule a 30-minute results review on 12/23.
[07:18] Dr. Sara Patel: thanks everyone.
[07:20] Alex Chen: thanks, talk soon.
next_steps: Send SOC 2 & ISO27001 cert PDFs and pen test report
Share SAML/SSO integration guide and RBAC matrix
Run 3-day benchmark using Parkway dev dataset (Priya to run) - target start 2027-12-20
